transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, my work physical is actually what got me here. 

The doctor doing the exam told me my weight is too low. I don't really agree with it, honestly. To me, I just feel lighter on my feet when I play basketball, and I'm not as weighed down when I'm working at the garage all day. But they told me I needed to come see someone about it, so here I am.
Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating and consume a very large amount of food in a short period, or do you ever use methods like vomiting or laxatives to influence your weight?

No, not at all. I don't ever eat a huge amount of food like that, or feel out of control with it. And I definitely don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything. I just... I just keep my portions pretty small, you know? But none of that other stuff.
Do you find yourself feeling very worried or anxious about the possibility of gaining weight?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, if I see the scale bump up even just a pound, or if my work jeans feel tighter, I start getting pretty anxious about it. I just start thinking I'm getting soft. And like I mentioned, I worry that I'll be slower moving around cars at the garage, or slower getting up and down the court. So, yeah, the thought of putting weight back on definitely bothers me.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see your body shape or weight differently than how others might describe it?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I just see myself. I know the doctor at my physical said I was too thin, but when I look in the mirror, I just see a guy who's lean and in shape. It's not like I look at myself and see a heavy guy staring back at me, if that's what you mean. I just see what's there.
Could you tell me a little bit about what your typical daily food intake looks like?

Well, most days I just stick to coffee in the morning. Then later on, maybe I'll have a small sandwich or just half of whatever food happens to be around. Things get pretty busy at the shop, and then there's always stuff going on at the house, so... I just feel better keeping things simple and sticking to my own rules for what I eat. It's just easier that way.
When you say you just see yourself as 'lean and in shape,' how do you reconcile that with the fact that your doctor flagged your weight as being low enough to be a medical concern?

I mean, I know people are worried about it, including that doctor, but... I just figure they’re making way too much of it. Look, I still show up for work every day at the shop, I take care of whatever needs doing around the house, and I'm still out there playing ball on the weekends. If it was really some big medical concern, I wouldn't be able to keep up with all that, you know? So I just think it's blown out of proportion.
Do you ever find yourself feeling dizzy, lightheaded, or unusually cold, especially during your shifts at the garage?

No, not really. I mean, the garage gets pretty drafty, so sure, I get cold sometimes, but... not unusually cold, you know? And I don't get dizzy or lightheaded while I'm working. Like I said, I'm keeping up with everything just fine.
If you were to increase your portion sizes to reach the weight your doctor recommends, what is the primary reason that feels difficult or distressing for you?

Well, honestly, it's just... I really don't want to gain weight. If I see the scale bump up even a pound, or if my jeans start feeling tighter, I just start thinking I'm getting soft. And if I get soft, I'm going to be slower—slower moving around the cars at the shop, slower getting up and down the court on the weekends. I just don't want to lose my edge, you know? So the idea of eating more and putting on weight... it just messes with my head.

Even though you feel you are performing well at work and in sports, are you able to acknowledge that your current body weight might be medically dangerous or significantly below a healthy range for your height?

Look, I know what the doctor said, and I know people are worried about it. But... I just don't see it as being dangerous. Like I said before, I figure they're just making way too much of it. I'm still showing up for work every single day, I take care of everything that needs doing at home, and I'm still playing ball on the weekends. If my weight was actually medically dangerous, I wouldn't be able to do all that. So no, I really don't think it's dangerously low.
